text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London ended higher on technical buying by the funds and the trade. Most active May finished $3.60 higher at $307.50 per tonne, while August added $2.10 to close at $307.10 per tonne. Earlier, bullish sentiment in New York spilled over into the London market. In New York raw sugar futures ended firmer across the board. Aggressive trade buying in the second-position May contract was noted with just two weeks remaining before the March expiry. Fund buying in May and selling in March was also cited. March and May ended 14 points higher at 10.92 and 10.88 cents/lb respectively. News that the Philippines will import at least 500,000 tonnes in 1997/98 and that tax-free sugar exports in Brazil are still under study could aid sentiment on Wednesday.

PHILIPPINES - The Philippines is expected to import at least 500,000 tonnes of sugar in 1997/98 (September/August) to meet a projected local shortfall, Wilson Gamboa, head of the Sugar Regulatory Administration said. The reason is a anticipated fall in production to 1.7 million tonnes in 1997/98 from 1.8 million tonnes the previous year, Gamboa said. Other sources are estimating the 1996/97 crop at 1.9 million tonnes. If production next season should actually be as low as 1.7 million tonnes, the country would have an estimated supply deficit of roughly 560,000 tonnes, raw value. The Philippine sugar industry came into financial difficulties after excessive imports in 1995/96.

BRAZIL - Tax exemption for an extra 552,000 tonnes of Brazilian sugar exports this season is still under study, more than a month after the Ministry of Industry and Commerce authorized the sales, Pedro Cabral, head of the Sugar and Alcohol Department at the Ministry of Industry and Commerce said. Of the 552,318 tonnes 500,000 tonnes were allocated to the Center/South while the North-Northeast was allocated another 52,318 tonnes. The decision raised total free exports to 5,755,406 tonnes, tel quel, of which 4,181,088 tonnes for the Center/South and 1,547,318 tonnes of the North-Northeast. The delay in authorization was ascribed to lower world market and higher internal prices. Traders said the additional export quota will have little immediate effect because most mills have no produce left to ship. It was added that they are likely to either sell their quotas to other mills ore use them for the next crop.

THAILAND - In spite of the delayed start industry sources are still optimistic that Thai sugar production in 1996/97 (November/October) could reach 6.6 million tonnes, raw value, up from 6.323 million tonnes produced the previous year. Molasses production in 1996/97 is put at 2.97 million tonnes, up from 2.85 million tonnes the previous year.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong imported 285,492 tonnes of sugar, raw value, in calendar year 1996, 20 per cent more than was imported the previous year. Main suppliers of raw sugar in 1996 were Colombia (24,000 vs zero tonnes), China (10,342 vs 7,516 tonnes) and Thailand (12,000 vs 12,500 tonnes). Main suppliers of white sugar in 1996 were the UK (23,416 vs 22,030 tonnes), China (21,948 vs 19,747 tonnes), South Korea (131,727 vs 116,086 tonnes) and Australia (27,084 vs 32,356 tonnes). The country exported 80,533 tonnes of sugar, raw value, in 1996, up from 67,079 tonnes exported in 1995.
